climbing_route.label: Off-trail scramble to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Leave the trail for the off-trail scramble to the summit. No further description of the scramble itself is on file.

climbing_route.label: Right-hand gully from the southwest spur
climbing_route.notes: From the southwest spur at approximately 6,900 ft, the route-finding crux: locate a gully system cut into the rock face and, of two narrow parallel channels about 30 feet apart, take the RIGHT-hand one. Ascend the narrowing gully, which opens into broken rock, to gain the crest of the south ridge. The rock here is notoriously loose and crumbly by Cascades standards; helmets are strongly recommended and parties should keep group size small (6 or fewer) and spread out to manage rockfall risk to those below.

climbing_route.label: South ridge crest to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Follow the ridge crest, favoring the west side, to the summit. A faint boot path and scattered cairns mark much of this stretch but both disappear for long sections, so be prepared to route-find. The upper ridge rock is loose and crumbly.

wa_mount_mystery_standard.skip_reason: The approach text stops at the base of the climb: "then up basins/gullies (via the Mystery Glacier or the south ridge) to the base of the summit block." Nothing on file describes the summit block itself.

climbing_route.label: Blue Glacier to Snow Dome and the upper mountain
climbing_route.notes: From the glacier's edge it is roughly 4-6 more miles and about 3,700 ft of gain, roped up for crevasse travel, up to Snow Dome (~6,600 ft) and the upper mountain. A notable hazard en route is a large crevasse near Crystal Pass that is often 'impassable' except via a snow bridge that must be scouted each season. July-September is the best window for a straightforward glacier crossing.

climbing_route.label: Rocky gully to the 4,300 ft basin
climbing_route.notes: From the boot path the route rises via a rocky gully to a small basin around 4,300 ft, then continues into a basin east of the summit near 5,400 ft.

climbing_route.label: Final snow/rock gully to the ridge
climbing_route.notes: From the basin east of the summit near 5,400 ft, the final snow/rock gully leads to the summit ridge.

climbing_route.label: Ridge crest to the true (south) summit
climbing_route.notes: The ridge crest to the true (south) summit is mostly Class 2 with occasional Class 3, and an exposed knife-edge section reported by some parties.

climbing_route.label: East ridge to the summit
climbing_route.notes: From the high camp (commonly Lone Tree Pass) below Pulitzer and Mount Ferry, the east ridge is scrambled to the summit. No further description of the ridge is on file.

climbing_route.label: Lower third of the SE ridge
climbing_route.notes: The lower third of the SE ridge is mostly 2nd-class scrambling on crumbly rock and heather, until it becomes impassable.

climbing_route.label: Scree traverse around the cliff band
climbing_route.notes: Where the ridge becomes impassable, drop a few hundred feet to traverse steep, firm scree around 5,300 ft on the east side to bypass a cliff band.

climbing_route.label: Upper ridge and summit snow slope
climbing_route.notes: Regain the ridge for an easy 2nd-class scramble around its west side, then a moderately steep snow slope on the east side leads to the summit. Microspikes and an axe have been used here even in late August.

climbing_route.label: Standard gully on the south side
climbing_route.notes: From Rahm's south side, ascend one of three gullies dropping from the summit; the standard gully is loose 3rd class with an exposed knife-edge snow arete partway up.

climbing_route.label: Climbers' trail to the top
climbing_route.notes: The gully leads to a well-defined climbers' trail leading to the top.
